I have written a lot of tiny files to an SSD from Ubuntu, that SSD is not the system's root drive.
I usually run Windows on that SSD. Is the drive now automatically TRIMmed while running Windows or should I execute fstrim in Linux manually?

It should be fine, TRIM should be enabled in Windows. You can check with a simple command in Windows, it is easily searchable. If the SSD is formatted NTFS I would let Windows do it, just to be safe. Also, remember to have backups of the data you want to keep.

Thanks. I do have backups. I was just unsure whether TRIM needs to be called on specific sections of the SSD directly after deletion. But seeing as you can just start it generally in a cron job, it should be fine.
TRIM was enabled by default when I installed Manjaro on my SSD.
Any way to check this? I have the same situation so its probably enabled but id like to make sure...

Check your /etc/fstab file.

cat /etc/fstab

You'll need to know what drive UUID corresponds to your SSD, but if it has discard under <options> that means TRIM is enabled for that drive.
